documents.author: transplant surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL TRANSPLANT CENTER - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 12/24/2020, discharged 12/29/2020.

Procedure 12/24/2020: deceased donor kidney transplant, graft placed in the left iliac fossa with ureteroneocystostomy and ureteral stent. Native right polycystic kidney left in situ (left native removed 2011).

Course: prompt graft function, no dialysis needed after surgery. Creatinine down to 1.1 by discharge. Stent to come out in clinic at about 4 weeks.

Discharge medications:
- tacrolimus 5 mg PO BID, trough goal 8-10 ng/mL
- mycophenolate mofetil 750 mg PO BID
- prednisone 5 mg daily (after steroid taper)
- trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole SS 1 tab daily (PJP prophylaxis x 6 months)
- amlodipine 10 mg daily
- aspirin 81 mg daily
- insulin glargine 24 units qhs; insulin lispro 1 unit/12 g carbohydrate with meals
Allergies: NKDA

Follow-up: transplant clinic twice weekly with labs for the first month. Hemodialysis discontinued; dialysis unit notified.

events.reason: decreased urine output and edema two weeks after kidney transplant

reports.text: Specimen: transplant kidney, percutaneous needle core biopsy. Two cores with adequate cortex. Interstitial mononuclear cell infiltrate with tubulitis and tubular epithelial injury. Glomeruli and arteries without significant abnormality. C4d immunostain negative.
reports.conclusion: Acute T-cell-mediated rejection of the renal allograft.

documents.title: Transplant nephrology discharge summary
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
TRANSPLANT NEPHROLOGY - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 1/7/2021, discharge 1/12/2021.

Reason: 45M, deceased donor renal transplant 12/24/2020 for ADPKD, readmitted about two weeks out with falling urine output, fatigue and new swelling of both legs.

On arrival BP 160/95, T 37.2 C. Mild bilateral leg edema; graft in the LLQ tender to palpation. Creatinine 3.2 (discharge baseline 1.1), BUN 46, K 5.8. UA: 1+ protein, WBC casts on microscopy.

Graft biopsy 1/8: interstitial mononuclear infiltrate with tubular injury, read as acute T-cell-mediated rejection.

Treatment: IV methylprednisolone pulse daily x3, then resumed prednisone 5 mg daily. Tacrolimus level 8.9, dose unchanged. Hyperkalemia managed with dietary restriction and binder in hospital; K normal by day 3. Urine output recovered; creatinine falling at discharge.

Discharge meds unchanged from transplant discharge. Allergies NKDA.
Problems: acute rejection (treated), hyperkalemia (resolved), ADPKD, DM2, HTN.
Follow-up: transplant clinic in 3 days with labs.

documents.title: Video Visit - post-discharge
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at home in South Hadley, identity verified.

Transplant 12/24, then readmitted 1/7-1/12 for acute cellular rejection, got 3 days of IV steroid pulses. Back on prednisone 5. Transplant clinic labs yesterday: creatinine down to 1.2 per their portal (he read it to me). Making good urine, legs no longer swollen. Sugars ran 250-300 on the pulses, back to 140-190 now; took extra lispro per ratio, no lows.

Meds reconciled against transplant discharge: tacrolimus 5 BID, MMF 750 BID, pred 5, TMP-SMX SS daily, amlodipine 10, ASA 81, glargine 24 qhs, lispro ratio. NKDA.

A/P: rejection treated, graft function back near baseline - transplant nephrology following closely. Hyperkalemia resolved. DM - steroid bump resolved, no change. Out of work on leave until transplant team clears him. COVID vaccine: transplant team wants him to get it when eligible; he's on the list. In-person visit in 6-8 weeks.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN RECORD

CC: R flank pain, blood in urine.
HPI: 45M with ADPKD, deceased donor kidney 10 weeks ago (graft LLQ), on tacrolimus/MMF/prednisone. Two days of escalating right flank pain and urine that turned red today. Also a dull frontal headache since this morning. No fever, no dysuria. FH notable for kidney disease - father on dialysis in his 50s.

Meds per pt list: tacrolimus 5 BID, MMF 750 BID, prednisone 5, TMP-SMX SS, amlodipine 10, ASA 81, glargine 24, lispro. NKDA.

Exam: BP 160/100. Uncomfortable but nontoxic. Large firm right flank mass, tender. Graft site nontender. Neuro nonfocal.

UA: blood and protein; microscopy RBC present without casts.
Renal US: large cysts throughout the right native kidney; transplant looks normal, no hydro.
MRI brain (headache, family hx of ruptured aneurysm): 4 mm ACom saccular aneurysm, no bleed.

MDM: hematuria and flank pain most consistent with a bleed into a native-kidney cyst in ADPKD; graft not involved, creatinine at his baseline. Unruptured intracranial aneurysm, incidental to a benign-feeling headache that improved here with acetaminophen.

Dispo: home. Acetaminophen for pain, no NSAIDs. Hydrate. Return for fever, clots, retention, worst headache or neuro change. Genetic testing for ADPKD sent after discussion with transplant nephrology on call. Referral placed to neurovascular surgery. PCP f/u this week.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit - post ED
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First in-person visit since transplant. Seen in ED 3/1 for R flank pain and bloody urine - felt to be a bleeding cyst in the old right kidney. Urine cleared by the next afternoon, pain now a 2/10 ache, acetaminophen twice yesterday. Headache gone.

The bigger worry for him is the aneurysm on the MRI - his dad died of one at 58. Spent most of the visit on this. Explained what 4 mm means and that it hasn't bled; the decision about watching vs treating belongs with neurovascular surgery and he should hear it from them. I made sure the referral is moving; ED placed one too, consolidating.

Exam: BP improved from ED, as charted. R flank full, mildly tender. Graft nontender. Neuro intact.

A/P:
1. Unruptured ACom aneurysm - neurovascular referral. BP control matters; amlodipine 10 continued. He is already off cigarettes.
2. Native cyst hemorrhage, resolved - acetaminophen only.
3. Transplant - followed by transplant nephrology; genetics pending.
Return precautions for thunderclap headache reviewed. Back to teaching next week.

documents.title: Neurovascular surgery consultation
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
NEUROVASCULAR SURGERY - CONSULTATION

Thank you for referring Mr. Murphy, 45, with ADPKD and a recent kidney transplant, for an incidentally found aneurysm.

Imaging reviewed: 4 mm saccular aneurysm of the anterior communicating artery, unruptured, regular contour.

History: father with polycystic kidney disease died of a ruptured cerebral aneurysm at 58. Former smoker, quit December 2019. Hypertension on amlodipine. NKDA.

Exam: alert, fluent, cranial nerves intact, strength and coordination normal.

Discussion: we talked at length about endovascular or open treatment versus surveillance. Family history and ADPKD raise his risk; the small size, regular shape and his recent transplant (with procedural and anesthetic risks while still early on immunosuppression) favor watching for now. After discussion he prefers surveillance.

Plan: MRA (non-contrast time-of-flight) in 6 months, then yearly if unchanged. Blood pressure control and continued tobacco abstinence. Seek emergency care for sudden severe headache. We will revisit treatment if it grows or changes shape.

documents.title: Bloody diarrhea, vomiting
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pt called before school. A week of crampy belly pain, vomiting on and off, and now diarrhea with blood several times a day. No travel, nobody sick at home. Transplant recipient 3.5 months out on MMF/tac/pred.
This needs a same-day transplant evaluation, not a school day. Advised he call the transplant coordinator now and go to the transplant center ED if he can't be seen today; if lightheaded or bleeding heavier, 911. He agreed. I left a message for the transplant coordinator as well.

documents.title: Gastroenterology discharge summary
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY INPATIENT SERVICE - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 4/12/2021, discharged 4/19/2021.

45M, ADPKD, deceased donor kidney 12/2020 complicated by early acute rejection, recent native-cyst hematuria. One week of abdominal pain, emesis and bloody stools. Denied travel or sick contacts.

Admission: afebrile, BP 130/85, HR 88. Abdomen diffusely tender, no rebound or guarding.
Labs: Hgb 12.1, WBC 9.0 with normal differential, plt 250, Cr 1.2 (his post-transplant baseline), LFTs normal. CMV PCR 185,000 IU/mL.

Colonoscopy 4/13: multiple large, shallow ulcers through the colon, biopsied. Pathology: CMV inclusions, CMV immunostain positive.

Dx: CMV colitis in a kidney transplant recipient.

Treatment: IV ganciclovir (renally dosed) 4/13-4/18 with resolution of bleeding and tolerance of diet, transitioned to oral valganciclovir 900 mg BID. Immunosuppression continued per transplant nephrology. Tacrolimus level in range.

Discharge meds: valganciclovir 900 mg BID (NEW), tacrolimus 5 BID, MMF 750 BID, prednisone 5, TMP-SMX SS daily, amlodipine 10, ASA 81, glargine 24 qhs, lispro per ratio. NKDA.

Follow-up: weekly CMV PCR and CBC via transplant clinic; duration of valganciclovir per transplant ID/nephrology once viral load is undetectable.

documents.title: Post-discharge visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 3 days after discharge for CMV colitis. Stools formed, no blood since 4/16. Eating normally. Tired. Taking valganciclovir 900 BID - pharmacy needed a PA for the quantity, which our office and the transplant center both submitted; approved yesterday.

Meds reconciled; valganciclovir added. NKDA.
Exam: looks tired, afebrile. Abd soft, minimal LLQ tenderness near graft? he says that's the colon, no different from before. No edema.

A/P: CMV colitis on treatment - transplant team checking PCR weekly. Watch counts on valganciclovir (their labs). Genetic test from the ED still pending. Neurovascular plan noted (MRA in Sept). He is not back at school yet. RTC 1 month, sooner prn.

documents.body:
TRANSPLANT NEPHROLOGY CLINIC
Visit 4/28/2021

Dear colleague,

I saw Joel today, four months after his deceased donor kidney transplant for ADPKD-related end-stage kidney disease, and two weeks after discharge for CMV colitis. He has no complaints and reports taking every dose of tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisone. Valganciclovir continuing.

BP 132/86. Exam unremarkable; graft nontender.

Labs: creatinine 2.8 mg/dL, up from his 1.2 baseline at the time of the CMV admission. BUN 44. Urinalysis without protein or blood. Tacrolimus trough 8.4, in range.

Genetic testing (sent from the ED in March) returned: heterozygous pathogenic variant in PKD1, consistent with his clinical ADPKD. Genetic counseling information given for his family.

We will see him back with labs.

Medication list: tacrolimus 5 mg BID, mycophenolate 750 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, valganciclovir 900 mg BID, TMP-SMX SS daily, amlodipine 10 mg, aspirin 81 mg, insulin glargine 24 units, insulin lispro per ratio. NKDA.

Transplant Nephrology

medications.reason: CMV treatment course complete, PCR undetectable

Main renal artery and vein patent with normal waveforms; resistive indices normal. Normal parenchymal perfusion on color imaging.
reports.conclusion: Patent transplant vessels with normal perfusion. No obstruction.

reports.text: Specimen: transplant kidney, needle core biopsy, two cores. Interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy with mononuclear inflammation in fibrotic areas and tubulitis. Arteries without vasculitis. C4d negative. No viral cytopathic change.
reports.conclusion: Chronic active T-cell-mediated rejection with interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy.

TRANSPLANT NEPHROLOGY - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 5/12/2021 (via ED), discharge 5/17/2021.

Presentation: malaise, falling urine output, mild graft tenderness, no fever. BP 158/98. Firm, slightly enlarged allograft. Creatinine 3.9. Duplex ultrasound normal vessels and perfusion, no obstruction.

Biopsy 5/13: chronic active T-cell-mediated rejection with IFTA. C4d negative.

Treatment: IV methylprednisolone pulses, then prednisone back to 5 mg daily; tacrolimus continued with trough 8-10 goal (8.7 on admission). Creatinine improving at discharge.

CMV PCR not detected on admission; valganciclovir course completed and stopped at discharge per transplant ID.

Discharge meds: tacrolimus 5 BID, MMF 750 BID, prednisone 5, TMP-SMX SS, amlodipine 10, ASA 81, glargine 24, lispro per ratio. Valganciclovir STOPPED. NKDA.
Problems: chronic allograft rejection; CMV colitis, treated; ADPKD; DM2; HTN.
Follow-up: transplant clinic weekly x4 with labs.

documents.title: Post-discharge visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Third admission since the transplant. Biopsy showed chronic rejection; steroid pulses again. Discouraged today - asked whether the kidney will last. Told him honestly that transplant nephrology is the right team to answer that, and that his creatinine has been coming down at every check since the biopsy.

Glucose ran high on the pulses, now settling. Off valganciclovir. Bowels normal.

Exam: BP as charted. No edema. Graft mildly tender.

A/P: chronic allograft rejection - per transplant. CMV colitis resolved. DM - no changes. HTN - amlodipine 10. Mood: frustrated and worn out but not depressed, sleeping fine; PHQ-2 1. Encouraged the transplant social worker. Finishing the school year remotely. RTC 2 months.
